subject: Political Science
central_question: How can nationalism create collective identity and political freedom without turning cultural difference into exclusion, separatism or conflict?
in_scope_units: Introducing Nationalism through unification, anti-colonial liberation, empire break-up and separatist conflict.
Nations and Nationalism through imagined community, shared beliefs, history, territory and political ideals.
Common Political Identity and the democratic case against compulsory cultural uniformity.
National Self-Determination, statehood, one-culture–one-state, the Basque example and minority problems.
Nationalism and Pluralism through group rights, inclusive identity, democracy and Tagore’s critique.
banned_topics: Detailed citizenship acquisition and refugee law, which belong to Citizenship.
Detailed religious domination and models of secularism, which belong to Secularism.
Detailed constitutional division of powers, which belongs to Federalism in the Indian Constitution at Work textbook.

known_pitfalls.claim: Nationalism always unites and liberates people.
known_pitfalls.correction: It can also divide, exclude, displace and generate bitterness, war and separatist conflict.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every nation must share one language, religion or descent.
known_pitfalls.correction: No single cultural feature is common to all nations; nations are imagined communities built through shared beliefs and aspirations.
The chapter favours shared political ideals and equal citizenship over compulsory religion, race or language.

known_pitfalls.claim: Self-determination always requires a separate sovereign state.
known_pitfalls.correction: It can be reinterpreted through democratic rights, autonomy, recognition and equality within an existing state.

known_pitfalls.claim: Patriotism should override every other moral concern.
known_pitfalls.correction: Tagore supports independence but warns that patriotism must not triumph over humanity.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise Q3 on nationalism’s unifying and divisive effects.
Use NCERT Exercise Q1 to distinguish a nation from family, clan and other groups.
Use NCERT Exercise Q4 to reject one universal cultural test of nationhood.
Use NCERT Exercise Q2 to assess national self-determination and statehood.
Conclude with NCERT Exercise Q6 on democratic responses to nationalist aspirations.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises contain Questions 1–7 on nationhood, self-determination, nationalism’s effects, cultural factors, nationalist feeling, democracy and limitations.
